plan/dispatch
SQLite libra.db

PR replay microVM

Builds base/head, runs tests,
replays traffic, no LLM

A1 HTTPS webhook: pull_request
(HMAC-checked) (async)

A2/C2 SQL: gate audit, run rows,
reply jobs (local)
A3 Fly Machines API: create run-once VM (sync)
A4 HTTPS: fetch base/head source (sync)
A5 HTTPS /internal callback: evidence (HMAC) (sync)

A6 Checks API: Check Run + line
comments (sync)
Gates then dispatch

Repo allowlist, draft, base branch and risk gates are audited; skipped
PRs get no check. The VM runs build, tests, base/head replay and posts
evidence back.
Source: api/src/routes/webhooks.ts, api/src/services/pr-sandbox.ts
Advisory and isolated

Verdicts never block merge. Callback is HMAC-checked; writes are
skipped unless the DB is provably local.
Source: api/src/routes/pr-sandbox-callback.ts, api/src/services/db-isolation.ts

Truthful ack
Ingest authenticates the key, awaits the ClickHouse insert, and returns 429/503 with Retry-After rather than dropping spans. Readers filter producer_origin='customer'.

Conversation agent

Credentialless Codex Slack
turns via one leased job
capability
C1 Events API: thread reply (signed) (async)

A2/C2 SQL: gate audit, run rows,
reply jobs (local)

C3 Responses API: stateless
reply turn + tools (sync)
C4 chat.postMessage: terminal thread reply (sync)
HTTPS /internal: lease job, MCP reads, terminal (sync)
codex exec: resume persistent thread turn (sync)

Interaction view · columns = actors; frames = trust/deployment boundaries; vertical lines identify actors, not calls. Read labeled arrows caller → recipient, response included. Solid = sync
request; dashed = async delivery; dotted = local I/O. Numbered stages define order; equal stages are alternatives; unnumbered calls are independent.
Two responders, one job

Each turn is a general_question job. Prod uses the in-process stateless responder; the
Codex worker is the alternate and leases jobs without Slack or DB credentials.
Source: api/src/services/conversation-responder-tick.ts, conversation-agent/src/worker.ts
Terminal is final

A send accepted by the host is final; ambiguous delivery settles as delivery_unknown and is
never resent.
Source: api/src/services/slack-reply-executor.ts
